routing_warnings.description: The requirement that newly created sets match the intended style and remain consistent between shots specifically concerns set visual continuity.
The client's comparison verifies improved similarity among the set images, not project-wide artistic-style stability.
In the supplied context, the client's statement that the new images look significantly better concerns the set-image revisions.
Combining preferred character details with a target style is specific to the character-design Requirement.
The reported shifting style and requested rougher graffiti aesthetic explicitly concern the three characters and should not be broadened to project-wide style consistency.
The rougher, darker, sketch-like target is a character-specific visual-style attribute.
The proposed restyling of all three characters and recreation of their frames belongs to the character visual-style Requirement.

The concern about achieving and further refining the desired look is better handled under the character visual-style Requirement; the separate animation-quality clause belongs to REQ_ANIMATION_QUALITY.
This message concerns general artistic-style drift across the project rather than the character-specific appearance target.
The request to restore missing character shadows belongs to the independently defined character-shadows Requirement.
The observed absence of shadows in the revised renders is runtime evidence for the character-shadows Requirement.
The separate clauses about desired animation quality and further animation testing also concern the animation-quality Requirement.
The requirement that newly created sets match the intended style and remain consistent between shots belongs to set visual continuity.
The client's observation concerns increased visual similarity between the sets rather than raw image quality.
The concern about achieving the desired overall look concerns artistic style rather than set-image resolution or quality.
The separate concern about whether the desired animation quality can be achieved belongs to the animation-quality Requirement.
This message concerns the maximum achievable quality of the supplied set images rather than shot-to-shot set continuity.
The client discusses changing shot angles to improve set-image resolution, which concerns image quality rather than visual continuity.
The proposal to generate new starting images is motivated by inadequate set-image quality rather than continuity itself.
The client's broad observation that the new images look significantly better most directly supports improved image quality and does not specifically verify set continuity.
The proposed angle changes are conditional on improving set-image resolution and primarily concern the set-image quality Requirement.
This message defers the independently tracked opening aerial establishing shot rather than changing general shot-direction accuracy.
The paired Q and Deadwax frame counts and wide-to-close progression belong to the independently specified CC1 framing sequence.
